Then $p({xs}) = ({y0})({L0:texfrac}) + ({y1})({L1:texfrac}) + ({y2})({L2:texfrac}) =$ **{val:frac}**.

drills.title: Newton form coefficients
drills.prompt: Write the quadratic through $({x0}, {y0})$, $({x1}, {y1})$ and $({x2}, {y2})$ in Newton form $p(x) = c_0 + c_1(x {nx0:signed}) + c_2(x {nx0:signed})(x {nx1:signed})$. Find $c_0$, $c_1$ and $c_2$.

drills.title: Recover a shared secret
drills.prompt: A secret $S$ is the constant term of a quadratic $p(x) = S + ax + bx^2$. Three shares are $(1, {y1})$, $(2, {y2})$ and $(3, {y3})$. Find $S = p(0)$.
drills.solution: At $x = 0$ the Lagrange basis values for $x = 1, 2, 3$ are $3$, $-3$ and $1$, so $S = 3y_1 - 3y_2 + y_3 = {t1} - {t2} + {y3} =$ **{s}**.

drills.title: A linear fractional function as a transformed 1/x
drills.prompt: Write $f(x) = \dfrac{ {a:coef}x {b:signed} }{ x {d:signed} }$ in the form $f(x) = \dfrac{k}{x - h} + v$. Find $h$, $v$ and $k$.
drills.solution:
Divide: ${a:coef}x {b:signed} = {a}(x {d:signed}) + ({kk})$, so $f(x) = {a} + \dfrac{ {kk} }{x {d:signed}}$.
So $h =$ **{hh}**, $v =$ **{vv}**, $k =$ **{kk}**: the graph of $\tfrac1x$ stretched by $k$ and centered at $({hh}, {vv})$.

drills.title: Use the center of symmetry
drills.prompt: For $f(x) = \dfrac{ {a:coef}x {bb:signed} }{ x {nh:signed} }$, you are told that $f({x1}) = {y1:texfrac}$. Use the center of symmetry (no substitution) to find $f({x2})$. Give an exact answer.
drills.solution:
The asymptotes are $x = {hh}$ and $y = {a}$, so the center is $({hh}, {a})$. The inputs ${x1}$ and ${x2}$ are both {s} units from ${hh}$, so $f({x1}) + f({x2}) = 2({a}) = {twov}$.
Then $f({x2}) = {twov} - \left({y1:texfrac}\right) =$ **{y2:frac}**.

drills.title: Thin-lens image distance
drills.prompt: A thin lens has focal length {fl} cm. An object is {dob} cm from the lens. Use $d_i = \dfrac{f\,d_o}{d_o - f}$ to find the image distance (to 1 decimal place; negative means a virtual image) and the magnification $m = -\dfrac{d_i}{d_o}$ (to 2 decimal places).
drills.solution:
$d_i = \dfrac{ ({fl})({dob}) }{ {dob} - {fl} } = \dfrac{ ({fl})({dob}) }{ {diff} } \approx$ **{di:num1} cm**.
$m = -\dfrac{d_i}{d_o} \approx$ **{mag:num2}** (negative: the image is upside down; positive: upright and virtual).

drills.title: From sinh x to cosh x and x
drills.prompt: Given $\sinh x = \dfrac{ {sn} }{ {sd} }$, find $\cosh x$ (exact fraction) and $x$ (4 decimal places).
drills.solution: $\cosh^2 x = 1 + \sinh^2 x = 1 + \left(\dfrac{ {sn} }{ {sd} }\right)^2$, and $\cosh x > 0$, so $\cosh x =$ **$\dfrac{ {cn} }{ {cd} }$**. Then $e^x = \cosh x + \sinh x = \dfrac{ {cn} }{ {cd} } + \dfrac{ {sn} }{ {sd} } = {ex:num4}$ (exactly $\tfrac{ {p} }{ {q} }$), so $x = \ln\tfrac{ {p} }{ {q} } \approx$ **{xv:num4}**.

drills.title: Solve sinh x = c
drills.prompt: Solve $\sinh x = {c}$. Round to 4 decimal places.
drills.solution: With $u = e^x$: $\dfrac{u - 1/u}{2} = {c}$, so $u^2 - 2({c})u - 1 = 0$ and $u = {c} \pm \sqrt{({c})^2 + 1}$. Only the plus sign gives $u > 0$: $e^x = {c} + {rt:num4} \approx {ux:num4}$. So $x = \ln\left({c} + \sqrt{({c})^2 + 1}\right) \approx$ **{xv:num4}**.

drills.title: Sag of a hanging cable
drills.prompt: A cable hangs in the shape $y = {a}\cosh\dfrac{x}{ {a} }$ (meters) between supports at $x = -{half}$ and $x = {half}$, a span of {span} m. How far below the supports is its lowest point? (Meters, 2 decimal places.)
drills.solution: At the supports $y = {a}\cosh\dfrac{ {half} }{ {a} } = {a}\cosh({ratio:num4}) \approx {a}({ch:num4})$; at the lowest point $x = 0$ and $y = {a}\cosh 0 = {a}$. Sag $= {a}\left(\cosh({ratio:num4}) - 1\right) \approx$ **{sag:num2}** m.

drills.title: When does a logistic model reach a level?
drills.prompt: For $P(t) = \dfrac{ {C:dp0} }{1 + {A}e^{-{k}t} }$, at what time $t$ does $P$ reach {target} ({pct}% of capacity)? Round to 2 decimal places.
drills.solution: Solve for $t$: $t = \dfrac1k\ln\dfrac{AP}{C - P} = \dfrac{1}{ {k} }\ln\dfrac{ {A} \cdot {target:dp0} }{ {rest:dp0} } = \dfrac{\ln({inside:num4})}{ {k} } \approx$ **{tv:num2}**.

drills.title: Growth rate from the logit
drills.prompt: A logistic process has carrying capacity {C}. It is at {P0} when $t = 0$ and at {P1} when $t = {T}$. Use the logit $\ln\dfrac{P}{C - P}$ to find $k$. (3 decimal places.)
drills.solution: Logits: $\ln\dfrac{ {P0:dp0} }{ {C:dp0} - {P0:dp0} } \approx {L0:num4}$ and $\ln\dfrac{ {P1:dp0} }{ {C:dp0} - {P1:dp0} } \approx {L1:num4}$. The logit is linear with slope $k$: $k = \dfrac{ {L1:num4} - ({L0:num4})}{ {T} } \approx$ **{kv:dp3}**.

drills.title: Carrying capacity from three points
drills.prompt: A quantity follows a logistic model. It is {P0:int} at $t = 0$, {P1:int} at $t = {h}$ and {P2:int} at $t = 2 \cdot {h}$. Find the carrying capacity $C$.
drills.solution: Take reciprocals $y_n = 1/P_n$; they follow $y_n = c + Bq^n$ with $c = 1/C$. The differences give $q = \dfrac{y_2 - y_1}{y_1 - y_0} = \dfrac{1}{ {m} }$. Then $B = \dfrac{y_1 - y_0}{q - 1}$ and $c = y_0 - B = \dfrac{1}{ {Cv:dp0} }$. Equivalently, $C = \dfrac{P_1(P_0P_1 + P_1P_2 - 2P_0P_2)}{P_1^2 - P_0P_2} = \dfrac{ {num:dp0} }{ {den:dp0} } =$ **{Cv}**.

drills.title: Count the digits of a power
drills.prompt: How many digits does ${b}^{ {n} }$ have?
drills.solution: $\log {b}^{ {n} } = {n}\log {b} \approx {lg:num4}$. A whole number $N$ has $\lfloor\log N\rfloor + 1$ digits, so ${b}^{ {n} }$ has **{dg}** digits.

drills.title: Largest exponential job in a time budget
drills.prompt: A computer does $10^{ {s} }$ operations per second. A job of size $n$ takes ${b}^n$ operations. What is the largest $n$ it can finish in {tt}?
drills.solution: The budget is $10^{ {s} } \times {ttv:dp0} = {budget:texsci}$ operations, with common log ${lgb:num4}$. We need ${b}^n \le$ budget, so $n \le \dfrac{ {lgb:num4} }{\log {b}} \approx {nexact:num4}$. The largest whole number is **{nmax}**.

drills.title: How many bisection steps?
drills.prompt: Bisection starts on an interval of width {w}. What is the smallest number of steps that makes the interval narrower than $10^{-{d}}$?
drills.solution: After $n$ steps the width is $\dfrac{ {w} }{2^n}$. We need $\dfrac{ {w} }{2^n} < 10^{-{d}}$, that is $2^n > {w} \times 10^{ {d} } = {ratio:dp0}$. Since $\log_2 {ratio:dp0} \approx {lg2:num4}$, the smallest whole $n$ is **{nn}**.

drills.title: Solve sin x = c on [0, 2π)
drills.prompt: Solve $\sin x = {c}$ on $[0, 2\pi)$. Give both solutions in radians to 3 decimal places, smaller first.
drills.solution: Principal value: $\alpha = \sin^{-1}({c}) \approx {al:num4}$. The partner is $\pi - \alpha$, and any negative angle gets $2\pi$ added. In $[0, 2\pi)$ the solutions are $x \approx$ **{x1:num4}** and $x \approx$ **{x2:num4}**.

drills.title: Solve cos x = c on [0, 2π)
drills.prompt: Solve $\cos x = {c}$ on $[0, 2\pi)$. Give both solutions in radians to 3 decimal places, smaller first.
drills.solution: Principal value: $\beta = \cos^{-1}({c}) \approx {be:num4}$, which is in $[0, \pi]$. The partner is $-\beta$; adding $2\pi$ puts it in the interval: $2\pi - \beta$. The solutions are $x \approx$ **{be:num4}** and $x \approx$ **{x2:num4}**.

drills.title: Multiple-angle equations
drills.prompt: For $\sin({B}x) = {c}$, find the smallest positive solution (radians, 3 decimal places) and the number of solutions in $[0, 2\pi)$.
drills.solution: Let $u = {B}x$. The smallest positive solution of $\sin u = {c}$ is $u = \sin^{-1}({c}) \approx {al:num4}$, so $x = \dfrac{ {al:num4} }{ {B} } \approx$ **{xs:num4}**. As $x$ runs over $[0, 2\pi)$, $u$ runs over $[0, {tb}\pi)$: {B} full turns with 2 solutions each, so **{n}** solutions.

drills.title: Amplitude-phase form
drills.prompt: Write ${a:coef}\sin x {b:signedcoef}\cos x$ as $R\sin(x + \varphi)$ with $R > 0$ and $-\pi < \varphi \le \pi$. Give $R$ (exact, like sqrt(13), or to 3 decimals) and $\varphi$ in radians to 3 decimal places.
drills.solution: $R = \sqrt{a^2 + b^2} = \sqrt{ {R2} } \approx$ **{R:num4}**. Then $\cos\varphi = \dfrac{ {a} }{\,R}$ and $\sin\varphi = \dfrac{ {b} }{\,R}$, so $\varphi$ is the direction of the point $({a}, {b})$; choose the angle in that point's quadrant (when the first coefficient is negative, add $\pi$ to the arctangent of the ratio and bring the result into $(-\pi, \pi]$): $\varphi \approx$ **{phi:num4}**.

drills.title: Range and period of a combined wave
drills.prompt: For $y = {a:coef}\sin({B:coef}x) {b:signedcoef}\cos({B:coef}x) {D:signed}$, find the maximum and minimum values (exact or 3 decimals) and the period (exact, like pi/2, or 3 decimals).
drills.solution: The two waves combine into one with amplitude $R = \sqrt{ {R2} } \approx {R:num4}$, so $y$ runs from ${D} - R$ to ${D} + R$: maximum **{mx:num4}**, minimum **{mn:num4}**. The period is $\dfrac{2\pi}{ {B} } \approx$ **{per:num4}**.

drills.title: Beats
drills.prompt: Two pure tones of equal loudness, {f1} Hz and {f2} Hz, sound together. How many beats per second are heard, and what is the frequency (in Hz) of the tone inside the beats?
drills.solution: $\sin(2\pi f_1 t) + \sin(2\pi f_2 t) = 2\cos\left(\pi(f_2 - f_1)t\right)\sin\left(\pi(f_1 + f_2)t\right)$. The beat frequency is $|f_2 - f_1| =$ **{d}** per second, and the tone is at the average frequency $\dfrac{ {f1} + {f2} }{2} =$ **{avg:num1}** Hz.

drills.title: Apply a matrix to a point
drills.prompt: The matrix $A = \begin{bmatrix} {a} & {b} \\ {c} & {d} \end{bmatrix}$ transforms the plane. Where does it send the point $({p}, {q})$?
drills.solution: Multiply the matrix by the column $\begin{bmatrix} {p} \\ {q} \end{bmatrix}$, row times column: the first row gives $({a})({p}) + ({b})({q}) = {xn}$ and the second row gives $({c})({p}) + ({d})({q}) = {yn}$. The image is **({xn}, {yn})**.

drills.title: Area of the image under a matrix
drills.prompt: A rectangle {w} units wide and {h} units tall is transformed by $A = \begin{bmatrix} {a} & {b} \\ {c} & {d} \end{bmatrix}$. What is the area of its image?
drills.solution: A linear transformation multiplies every area by $|\det A|$. Here $\det A = ({a})({d}) - ({b})({c}) = {dt}$, so the scale factor is {ad}. The rectangle has area ${w} \times {h} = {area0}$, so the image has area ${ad} \times {area0} =$ **{area}**.

drills.title: Two steps of a Markov chain
drills.prompt: A two-state Markov chain has transition matrix $P = \begin{bmatrix} {p} & {q} \\ {p2} & {q2} \end{bmatrix}$ (column $j$ lists the probabilities of moving from state $j$). Today the probability of state 1 is {s}, so $\mathbf{x}_0 = ({s}, {s2})$. What is the probability of state 1 two steps from now? Give the exact decimal.
drills.solution: One step: the first entry of $P\mathbf{x}_0$ is $({p})({s}) + ({q})({s2}) = {x1:dp3}$, so $\mathbf{x}_1 = ({x1:dp3}, {y1:dp3})$. Second step: $({p})({x1:dp3}) + ({q})({y1:dp3}) =$ **{x2:dp3}**.

drills.title: Steady state of a two-state chain
drills.prompt: Find the steady-state vector $(q_1, q_2)$ of the transition matrix $P = \begin{bmatrix} {p11} & {b} \\ {a} & {p22} \end{bmatrix}$ (columns add to 1). Give exact fractions.
drills.solution: Solve $(P - I)\mathbf{q} = \mathbf{0}$. The first row is $-{a}\,q_1 + {b}\,q_2 = 0$, so $q_1 = {ratio:texfrac}\,q_2$. With $q_1 + q_2 = 1$: $q_2 = {q2:texfrac}$ and $q_1 = {q1:texfrac}$. The steady state is **({q1:frac}, {q2:frac})**; check that $P\mathbf{q} = \mathbf{q}$.

drills.title: Eigenvalues of a 2×2 matrix
drills.prompt: Find the eigenvalues of $A = \begin{bmatrix} {a} & {b} \\ {c} & {d} \end{bmatrix}$. Enter the larger one first.
drills.solution: The trace is ${a} + ({d}) = {tr}$ and $\det A = ({a})({d}) - ({b})({c}) = {dt}$. The characteristic equation is $\lambda^2 {ntr:signedcoef}\lambda {dt:signed} = 0$, which factors as $(\lambda {nl1:signed})(\lambda {nl2:signed}) = 0$. The eigenvalues are **{l1}** and **{l2}** (check: they add to {tr} and multiply to {dt}).

drills.title: Eigenvector for a given eigenvalue
drills.prompt: The matrix $A = \begin{bmatrix} {a} & {b} \\ {c} & {d} \end{bmatrix}$ has eigenvalue $\lambda = {l1}$. Find the eigenvector of the form $(1, y)$. Give $y$ as an exact fraction or integer.
drills.solution: Solve $(A {nl1:signedcoef}I)\mathbf{v} = \mathbf{0}$. The first row of $A {nl1:signedcoef}I$ is $({am}, {b})$, so ${am:coef}x {b:signedcoef}y = 0$ (the second row is a multiple of it, because $\det(A {nl1:signedcoef}I) = 0$). With $x = 1$: ${am} {b:signedcoef}y = 0$, so ${b:coef}y = {nam}$ and $y =$ **{y:frac}**. Check: $A\begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ y \end{bmatrix} = {l1}\begin{bmatrix} 1 \\ y \end{bmatrix}$.

drills.title: Angle that removes the xy term
drills.prompt: Rotating the axes through an acute angle $\theta$ removes the $xy$ term from ${A:coef}x^2 {B:signedcoef}xy {C:signedcoef}y^2 = {G}$. Find $\theta$ in degrees, to 1 decimal place.
drills.solution: $\cot 2\theta = \dfrac{A - C}{\,B} = \dfrac{ {A} - ({C}) }{ {B} } \approx {ct:num4}$. For $0° < 2\theta < 180°$ this gives $2\theta \approx {tt:num2}°$, so $\theta \approx$ **{th:num1}°**. (A negative cotangent puts $2\theta$ between $90°$ and $180°$.)

drills.title: New coefficients after a rotation
drills.prompt: Rotate the axes through the acute angle $\theta$ with $\cot 2\theta = \dfrac{A - C}{\,B}$ to remove the $xy$ term from ${A:coef}x^2 {B:signedcoef}xy {C:signedcoef}y^2 = {G}$. The result is $A'x'^2 + C'y'^2 = {G}$. Find $A'$ and $C'$.
drills.solution:
$\cot 2\theta = \dfrac{ {A} - ({C}) }{ {B} } = {ct:texfrac}$, so $\cos 2\theta = {c2:texfrac}$ (same sign). Half-angle formulas: $\cos^2\theta = \dfrac{1 + \cos 2\theta}{2} = {cs:texfrac}$, $\sin^2\theta = {sn:texfrac}$, and $\sin\theta\cos\theta = \tfrac25$.

$A' = A\cos^2\theta + B\sin\theta\cos\theta + C\sin^2\theta = {A}\cdot{cs:texfrac} + ({B})\cdot\tfrac25 + ({C})\cdot{sn:texfrac} =$ **{Ap}**.

$C' = A\sin^2\theta - B\sin\theta\cos\theta + C\cos^2\theta = {A}\cdot{sn:texfrac} - ({B})\cdot\tfrac25 + ({C})\cdot{cs:texfrac} =$ **{Cp}**.

Check with the invariant: $A' + C' = {tot2} = A + C$.

drills.title: Focal radii of a point on an ellipse
drills.prompt: The point $P$ on the ellipse $\dfrac{x^2}{ {a2} } + \dfrac{y^2}{ {b2} } = 1$ has $x$-coordinate ${x0}$. Find its distances to the foci $F_1 = (-{c}, 0)$ and $F_2 = ({c}, 0)$. Give exact fractions or decimals to 2 places.
drills.solution: $a = {a}$ and $c = \sqrt{ {a2} - {b2} } = {c}$, so $e = \dfrac{\,c}{\,a} = {ecc:texfrac}$. The focal radii are $PF_1 = a + ex_0 = {a} + {ecc:texfrac}({x0}) =$ **${d1:texfrac} \approx {d1:num2}$** and $PF_2 = a - ex_0 = {a} - {ecc:texfrac}({x0}) =$ **${d2:texfrac} \approx {d2:num2}$**. Check: they add to $2a = {tot}$.

drills.title: Tangent line and focal distance of a parabola
drills.prompt: For the parabola $x^2 = {fp}y$, find the slope of the tangent line at $P = ({x0}, {y0})$, the $y$-intercept of that tangent line, and the distance from $P$ to the focus.
drills.solution: $4p = {fp}$, so $p = {p}$ and the focus is $(0, {p})$. The tangent to $x^2 = 4py$ at $(x_0, y_0)$ has slope $\dfrac{x_0}{2p} = \dfrac{ {x0} }{ {tp} } =$ **{m}** and meets the axis at $(0, -y_0)$, so the $y$-intercept is **{ny}**. The distance to the focus equals the distance to the directrix $y = -{p}$: $PF = y_0 + p = {y0} + {p} =$ **{fd}**.

drills.title: Perihelion and aphelion distances
drills.prompt: An object orbits the Sun on an ellipse with semi-major axis $a = {a:num1}$ AU and eccentricity $e = {ecc:num2}$. Find its perihelion and aphelion distances in AU (exact decimals).
drills.solution: The Sun is at a focus, $c = ae$ from the center. Perihelion: $a(1 - e) = {a:num1}({ome:num2}) =$ **{q:dp3}** AU. Aphelion: $a(1 + e) = {a:num1}({ope:num2}) =$ **{Q:dp3}** AU.

drills.title: Orbit size and shape from its closest and farthest points
drills.prompt: An object orbiting the Sun comes within {q:num1} AU of it and reaches {Q:num1} AU at its farthest. Find the semi-major axis $a$ (exactly) and the eccentricity $e$ (to 3 decimal places).
drills.solution: The major axis runs from perihelion to aphelion, so $a = \dfrac{q + Q}{2} = \dfrac{ {sm:num1} }{2} =$ **{a:num2}** AU, and $e = \dfrac{Q - q}{Q + q} = \dfrac{ {df:num1} }{ {sm:num1} } \approx$ **{ecc:dp3}**.

drills.title: Period from Kepler's third law
drills.prompt: An asteroid orbits the Sun with semi-major axis {a:num2} AU. Use Kepler's third law to find its period in years, to 2 decimal places.
drills.solution: With $T$ in years and $a$ in AU, $T^2 = a^3$, so $T = a^{3/2} = ({a:num2})^{3/2} \approx$ **{T:num2}** years. (Equivalently, $T = \sqrt{a^3}$.)

drills.title: Compute a cross product
drills.prompt: Find $\vec u \times \vec v$ for $\vec u = \langle {u1}, {u2}, {u3} \rangle$ and $\vec v = \langle {v1}, {v2}, {v3} \rangle$.
drills.solution:
Expand the determinant with rows $\mathbf{i}, \mathbf{j}, \mathbf{k}$; $\vec u$; $\vec v$ along the first row.
$\mathbf{i}$: $({u2})({v3}) - ({u3})({v2}) = {c1}$.
$\mathbf{j}$: $-\big[({u1})({v3}) - ({u3})({v1})\big] = -({j0}) = {c2}$.
$\mathbf{k}$: $({u1})({v2}) - ({u2})({v1}) = {c3}$.
So $\vec u \times \vec v =$ **$\langle {c1}, {c2}, {c3} \rangle$**. Check: dotting it with $\vec u$ or $\vec v$ gives 0.

drills.title: Area of a triangle in space
drills.prompt: Find the area of the triangle with vertices $A({ax}, {ay}, {az})$, $B({bx}, {by}, {bz})$ and $C({cx}, {cy}, {cz})$. (Exact like sqrt(41)/2, or 2 decimals.)
drills.solution:
Sides from $A$: $\vec{AB} = \langle {p1}, {p2}, {p3} \rangle$ and $\vec{AC} = \langle {q1}, {q2}, {q3} \rangle$.
Cross product: $\vec{AB} \times \vec{AC} = \langle {n1}, {n2}, {n3} \rangle$, with length $\sqrt{ {nn} }$.
The triangle is half the parallelogram: area $= \tfrac12\sqrt{ {nn} } \approx$ **{area:num2}**.

drills.title: Volume from the triple scalar product
drills.prompt: Find the volume of the parallelepiped spanned by $\vec u = \langle {u1}, {u2}, {u3} \rangle$, $\vec v = \langle {v1}, {v2}, {v3} \rangle$ and $\vec w = \langle {w1}, {w2}, {w3} \rangle$.
drills.solution:
The triple product $\vec u \cdot (\vec v \times \vec w)$ is the determinant with rows $\vec u, \vec v, \vec w$. Expanding along the first row:
$({u1})({m1}) - ({u2})({m2}) + ({u3})({m3}) = {det}$.
The volume is its absolute value: **{vol}**.

drills.title: Plane through three points
drills.prompt: Find the plane through $A({x0}, {y0}, {z0})$, $B({bx}, {by}, {bz})$ and $C({cx}, {cy}, {cz})$. Use the normal $\vec n = \vec{AB} \times \vec{AC}$ exactly as computed (don't divide out a common factor), and write the plane as $ax + by + cz = d$.
drills.solution:
$\vec{AB} = \langle {p1}, {p2}, {p3} \rangle$ and $\vec{AC} = \langle {q1}, {q2}, {q3} \rangle$, so $\vec n = \vec{AB} \times \vec{AC} = \langle {n1}, {n2}, {n3} \rangle$.
Point-normal form with $A$: ${n1}(x {mx:signed}) {n2:signed}(y {my:signed}) {n3:signed}(z {mz:signed}) = 0$.
Multiplying out: **${n1:coef}x {n2:signedcoef}y {n3:signedcoef}z = {rhs}$**. Check: $B$ and $C$ give {rhs} too.

drills.title: Distance from a point to a plane
drills.prompt: Find the distance from the point $({x1}, {y1}, {z1})$ to the plane ${pa:coef}x {pb:signedcoef}y {pc:signedcoef}z = {rhs}$. (Exact like 5/sqrt(14), or 2 decimals.)
drills.solution:
$D = \dfrac{\lvert ax_1 + by_1 + cz_1 - d \rvert}{\sqrt{a^2 + b^2 + c^2}}$.
Numerator: $({pa})({x1}) + ({pb})({y1}) + ({pc})({z1}) - ({rhs}) = {val}$, absolute value {num}.
Denominator: $\sqrt{ {nn} }$.
So $D = \dfrac{ {num} }{\sqrt{ {nn} }} \approx$ **{dist:num2}**.

drills.title: Where a line meets a plane
drills.prompt: Where does the line $x = {x0} {d1:signedcoef}t$, $y = {y0} {d2:signedcoef}t$, $z = {z0} {d3:signedcoef}t$ meet the plane ${pa:coef}x {pb:signedcoef}y {pc:signedcoef}z = {rhs}$? Give $t$ and the point.
drills.solution:
Substitute the line into the plane: ${pa}({x0} {d1:signedcoef}t) + ({pb})({y0} {d2:signedcoef}t) + ({pc})({z0} {d3:signedcoef}t) = {rhs}$.
Collect terms: ${k0} {nd:signedcoef}t = {rhs}$, so $t =$ **{t0}**.
Then the point is **$({xi}, {yi}, {zi})$**.

drills.title: Solve a first-order recurrence
drills.prompt: A sequence has $a_0 = {st}$ and $a_{n+1} = {rat:texfrac}\,a_n {add:signed}$. Find its fixed point $L$ and the term $a_{ {m} }$ (exact; fractions are fine).
drills.solution: The fixed point solves $L = {rat:texfrac}L {add:signed}$, so $L = \dfrac{ {add} }{1 - \left({rat:texfrac}\right)} =$ **${fix:texfrac}$**. The distance from $L$ is multiplied by ${rat:texfrac}$ each step, so $a_n = L + (a_0 - L)\left({rat:texfrac}\right)^n$ with $a_0 - L = {gap:texfrac}$. Then $a_{ {m} } = {fix:texfrac} + \left({gap:texfrac}\right)\left({rm:texfrac}\right) =$ **${am:texfrac}$**.

drills.title: Long-run level of a repeated dose
drills.prompt: A patient takes {dose} mg of a drug once a day. By the next day, {kp}% of the drug in the body remains. Let $A_n$ be the amount right after the $n$th dose, so $A_1 = {dose}$ and $A_{n+1} = {keep}A_n + {dose}$. Find $A_3$ and the long-run level (the fixed point), each to 1 decimal place.
drills.solution: $A_2 = {keep}({dose}) + {dose} = {a2:num2}$ and $A_3 = {keep}({a2:num2}) + {dose} =$ **{a3:num2} mg**. The fixed point solves $L = {keep}L + {dose}$: $L = \dfrac{ {dose} }{1 - {keep}} =$ **{lim:num2} mg**. Since $|{keep}| < 1$, the amounts approach this level.

drills.title: Solve a second-order recurrence
drills.prompt: Solve $a_n = {p:coef}a_{n-1} {q:signedcoef}a_{n-2}$ with $a_0 = {z0}$ and $a_1 = {z1}$. Write the answer as $a_n = A\,x_1^{\,n} + B\,x_2^{\,n}$, where $x_1 > x_2$ are the roots of the characteristic equation.
drills.solution: Trying $a_n = x^n$ gives $x^2 = {p:coef}x {q:signed}$, so the characteristic equation is $x^2 {mp:signedcoef}x {mq:signed} = 0$, with roots $x_1 =$ **{s}** and $x_2 =$ **{t}** (their sum is {p} and their product is {s}·({t})). Then $A + B = {z0}$ and $A({s}) + B({t}) = {z1}$, which give $A =$ **{cA}** and $B =$ **{cB}**. Check: the rule gives $a_2 = {p}({z1}) + ({q})({z0}) = {z2}$, and the formula gives ${cA}({s})^2 + ({cB})({t})^2 = {z2}$.

drills.title: Arrangements with repeated objects
drills.prompt: A signal is a row of {nr} identical red flags, {nb} identical blue flags and {ng} identical green flags ({tot} flags in all). How many different signals are possible?
drills.solution: Arrange {tot} flags, then divide out the orders of identical flags: $\dfrac{ {tot}! }{ {nr}!\,{nb}!\,{ng}! } = \dfrac{ {ft:dp0} }{ {nr}!\,{nb}!\,{ng}! } =$ **{ans:dp0}**.

drills.title: Identical objects into groups

choices.label: every child gets at least one

drills.prompt: In how many ways can {items} identical marbles be given to {kids} children if {mode}?
drills.solution: After first handing out one marble to each child when that is required, {left} marbles are left to share freely among {kids} children. Stars and bars: {left} stars and {km1} bars in {top} positions, so $\dbinom{ {top} }{ {km1} } =$ **{ans:dp0}**.

drills.title: Divisible by one number or another
drills.prompt: How many integers from 1 to {big} are divisible by {d1} or by {d2}? How many are divisible by neither?
drills.solution: Multiples of {d1}: $\lfloor {big}/{d1} \rfloor = {m1}$. Multiples of {d2}: ${m2}$. Numbers divisible by both are multiples of $\operatorname{lcm}({d1}, {d2}) = {l}$: ${m12}$, counted twice. So ${m1} + {m2} - {m12} =$ **{either}**, and ${big} - {either} =$ **{neither}** are divisible by neither.

drills.title: Probability of exactly k successes
drills.prompt: Each of {n} independent trials succeeds with probability {p}. What is the probability of exactly {k} successes? Give it to 4 decimal places.

drills.title: At least one success, and the mean
drills.prompt: Each of {n} independent trials succeeds with probability {p}. Find the probability of at least one success (to 4 decimal places) and the expected number of successes.
drills.solution: The complement of "at least one" is "none": $P(X = 0) = ({q})^{ {n} } \approx {qn:dp4}$, so $P(X \ge 1) = 1 - {qn:dp4} \approx$ **{P:dp4}**. The expected number is $np = {n}({p}) =$ **{mu:num2}**.

drills.title: Expected value of a dice game
drills.prompt: You pay \${cost} to roll a die. If the roll is {need} or higher you receive \${prize}; otherwise you receive nothing. What is your expected net gain per game, in dollars, to the nearest cent? (Negative means a loss.)
drills.solution: You win on {wins} of the 6 faces, so $P(\text{win}) = {pw:texfrac}$. The expected payout is ${prize} \cdot {pw:texfrac} \approx {payout:num2}$, and the cost is {cost}, so $E \approx {payout:num2} - {cost} =$ **{E:num2}** dollars per game.
